sentences.text: THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.482 CR.P.C PRAYING TO QUASH THE CHARGE SHEET IN C.C.NO.15435/2019 DATED 13.06.2019 ON THE FILE OF XXXII ADDL. C.M.M., BENGALURU FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 420 R/W 34 OF IPC FILED AGAINST THE PETITIONERS.

THIS CRL.P, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER Petitioners being accused Nos.1 and 2 in CC No.15435/2019 pending on the file of the learned 32nd Additional Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Bengaluru registered for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC R/w Section 34 of IPC, are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them.
2.

Heard Sri. Basavanna K.M., learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt. Rashmi Jadhav, learned Additional SPP for respondent No.1 and Sri. N.P.Amruthesh, Party-in-Person- respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
NC: 2024:KHC:45497 "Whether the petitioners have made out any grounds to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them?"

My answer to the above point is in 'negative' for the following:
REASONS 4. Respondent No.2 being the informant filed the first information with respondent No.1-police against accused Nos.1 to 9 alleging commission of the offence punishable under Section 420 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
Preliminary enquiry was held and later FIR came to be registered.
Investigation was under taken and the charge sheet came to be filed against accused Nos.1 and 2 only, while dropping accused Nos.2 to 9 named in the FIR.
Even though accused No.1 was not named in the FIR, charge sheet came to be filed against him.

sentences.text: It is the contention of the petitioners that the petitioners were working as President and Treasurer of the Karnataka Welfare Association for the blind.
Even earlier President and Treasurer have also accepted such donations from out of the CSR funds.
It is his contention that Rs. 33 lakhs said to have been received as donation as stated by the NC: 2024:KHC:45497 informant is already repaid.
Commission amount of Rs.13,36,500/- is also repaid by Pallavi Achar, who acted as commission agent.
The petitioners have never used this amount for personal use or benefit.
Therefore, contends that Section 420 of IPC could not have invoked against the petitioners.
6. The informant has filed the first information making specific allegations against all the nine accused persons.
Admittedly, the Karnataka Welfare Association for the blind is an NGO running with 100% funding by the State of Karnataka.

entities.text: Karnataka Welfare Association for the blind
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is stated that there is a bar for accepting donations from the general public.
Violating the said bar, the petitioners being the President and Treasurers accepted Rs.33 lakhs of donation and thereby, cheated the general public.
7. It is stated that the NGO is funded fully by the Government to take care of blind persons.

But the modus operandi adopted by the petitioners is that by showcasing the blind persons who are accommodated in the Society, are raising funds from various companies and individuals by misleading them.
The individuals and the companies are NC: 2024:KHC:45497 donating from out of CSR funds.
There are middle men who get 50% of the donation as commission.
Therefore, it is stated that on receipt of Rs.33 lakhs as donation, an amount of Rs.13,36,500/- was paid to one Pallavi Achar as commission.
This itself give rise to serious doubt about functioning of NGO.
8. The Investigating Officer after investigation filed the charge sheet.
However, dropped accused Nos.2 to 9 who are named in the FIR.
It is stated that the Pallavi referred to above who received commission of Rs.13,36,500/- is also dropped and she is said to be the witness on behalf of the prosecution.

She is cited as CW6.
9.

When admittedly, the petitioners being the president and treasurers of the NGO, accepted donation illegally and paid commission of Rs.13,36,500/-, the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the amount is already refunded or credited back will not serve any purpose.
Prima-facie, the offence in question is already committed.
More over, it is stated that the charge is already framed by the trial court and respondent No.2 is examined as PW1.
Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that there are no grounds to NC: 2024:KHC:45497 quash the criminal proceedings.
Petitioners have to face the trial.
Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Negative and process to pass the following:
ORDER The petition is Dismissed.
